nodes.content: Develop a semantic parser that distinguishes genuine utterance ambiguity from model uncertainty under unseen compositional structures.
requirements: Achieve ambiguity-detection F1 ≥0.85 on unseen compositions, using independently annotated sets of valid interpretations.
Match unambiguous-input execution accuracy of a single-output parser trained on identical data.

nodes.content: Freeze the baseline parser; train an interpretation-set ensemble to flag multiple valid parses supported across independently trained members.
Can cross-member support distinguish genuinely valid alternative parses from disagreement caused by unseen compositional structures?
Three-of-five support for distinct executable parses achieves ambiguity F1 ≥0.85 against independently annotated interpretation sets on unseen compositions.
Independently annotate held-out compositions; train five parsers on baseline data; calibrate three-member support; compare ambiguity F1 and unambiguous accuracy.
Build CompSplit-1: three annotators independently label valid executable interpretations for 600 held-out operator-combination utterances; adjudicate disagreements.
CompSplit-1 contains 600 held-out operator-combination utterances, three independent interpretation-set annotations each, and adjudicated executable gold sets.
Audit CompSplit-1 agreement and composition leakage; score three-of-five ambiguity F1 against gold sets and unambiguous execution against baseline.
CompSplit-1 audit found no leakage; three-of-five achieved 0.87 ambiguity F1 and 91% unambiguous execution versus baseline's 91%.
Select the three-of-five ensemble: CompSplit-1 ambiguity F1 reaches 0.87, while unambiguous execution matches the baseline at 91%.
Stratify CompSplit-1 by unseen operator pairing; compare ensemble false-positive rates with entropy-only ambiguity flags and baseline execution.
Pairing-balanced CompSplit-1 yielded 0.81 ambiguity F1 and 86% unambiguous execution versus baseline’s 91%, failing both targets.
Paraphrase-stable parse consensus with baseline fallback will reach pairing-balanced ambiguity F1 ≥0.85 while retaining 91% unambiguous execution.
Do meaning-preserving paraphrases retain the same valid interpretation sets for unseen operator pairings?
Gate ensemble ambiguity alerts by agreement across operator-preserving paraphrases; use the frozen baseline when the gate rejects ambiguity.
Independently validate operator-preserving paraphrases, tune the consensus gate, then evaluate pairing-balanced ambiguity F1 and baseline-relative unambiguous execution.
Using CompSplit-1 gold sets, independently validate paraphrases; compare ungated ensemble and paraphrase-gated fallback on pairing-balanced F1 and execution.
Independently validated paraphrase gating yielded pairing-balanced ambiguity F1 of 0.86 and unambiguous execution of 91%, versus ungated 0.81 and 86%.
Adopt paraphrase-gated fallback: pairing-balanced F1 rises from 0.81 to 0.86, and unambiguous execution recovers from 86% to 91%.
Freeze the adopted paraphrase gate and baseline fallback; independently annotate CompSplit-2 operator triples, then replicate ambiguity F1 and execution.
Collect 400 unseen operator-triple utterances; have three annotators independently enumerate executable interpretations and validate paraphrase equivalence.
CompSplit-2 contains 400 unseen operator-triple utterances, three independent interpretation-set annotations, adjudicated executable gold sets, and validated paraphrases.
Does paraphrase-consensus gating distinguish genuine ambiguity from ensemble disagreement on unseen operator triples without sacrificing unambiguous execution?
On CompSplit-2, the frozen gated parser achieves ambiguity F1 ≥0.85 and unambiguous execution ≥91%, matching the baseline.
Cluster parses by execution across counterfactual worlds; flag multiple paraphrase-stable clusters as ambiguous, otherwise retain baseline output.
Can counterfactual execution clusters separate genuinely distinct readings from equivalent parse variants on unseen operator triples?
Requiring distinct outputs in three counterfactual worlds reduces false ambiguity alerts while preserving CompSplit-2 ambiguity F1 ≥0.85.
On CompSplit-2, compare the frozen gate with three-world distinct-output clustering; score ambiguity F1, false-alert rate, and baseline-relative unambiguous execution.
CompSplit-2: gate achieved 0.86 F1 and 91% execution (baseline 91%); clustering cut false alerts 9%→6% but yielded 0.82 F1.
Requiring one paraphrase-stable, discriminative world instead of three preserves CompSplit-2 ambiguity F1 ≥0.85 and lowers false alerts below 9%.
Compare one-world paraphrase-stable and three-world clustering on CompSplit-2; report ambiguity F1, false-alert rate, and baseline-relative execution.
Paraphrase-stable world sampling raised three-world CompSplit-2 F1 from 0.82 to 0.85 (6% false alerts); one-world F1 was 0.83.
Audit one-world false negatives by operator triple on CompSplit-2; bootstrap ambiguity F1 and false-alert differences against the frozen gate.
One-world false alerts were 7% versus gate’s 9%; bootstrap F1 interval [0.79, 0.87] includes the 0.85 target.
Does three-world clustering preserve the baseline’s 91% unambiguous execution on CompSplit-2 despite residual false ambiguity alerts?
Compare three-world and one-world CompSplit-2 unambiguous execution against the 91% baseline; inspect overrides behind their 6% and 7% false-alert rates.
On CompSplit-2, measure three-world and one-world unambiguous execution against the 91% baseline; audit false-alert overrides and ambiguity F1.
Independently prevalidated discriminative-world selection raised one-world F1 from 0.83 to 0.85; false alerts remained 7%, execution matched baseline’s 91%.
Cascade paraphrase-consensus gating with prevalidated one-world discrimination; route rejected ambiguity alerts to the frozen baseline.
Does the cascade reduce CompSplit-2 false alerts below 7% while retaining ambiguity F1 ≥0.85 and unambiguous execution ≥91%?
The frozen cascade yields CompSplit-2 false alerts ≤6%, ambiguity F1 ≥0.85, and 91% unambiguous execution.
Lock cascade thresholds; evaluate CompSplit-2 against gated-only and one-world controls, then audit false alerts and unambiguous execution.
Run the locked cascade and both controls on CompSplit-2; bootstrap ambiguity F1, false-alert rate, and unambiguous execution.
CompSplit-2 cascade audit records locked predictions, gold interpretation sets, control outputs, and bootstrap intervals for F1, false alerts, and execution.
Verify cascade audit completeness; compare CompSplit-2 F1 and false alerts with controls, and unambiguous execution with the 91% baseline.
CompSplit-2 cascade achieved 0.85 ambiguity F1, 5% false alerts (gate 9%; one-world 7%), and 91% unambiguous execution (baseline 91%).
Distill the cascade into SingleSet using paraphrase-consistency and counterfactual-separation losses, preserving baseline outputs on unambiguous inputs.
Distill SingleSet from training-only cascade labels, freeze thresholds, then compare CompSplit-2 ambiguity F1 and unambiguous execution against cascade and baseline.
Using CompSplit-2 gold and locked cascade predictions, compare training-only-distilled SingleSet with cascade and baseline on ambiguity F1 and execution.
CompSplit-2 SingleSet achieved 0.86 ambiguity F1 and 91% unambiguous execution; cascade scored 0.85 and 91%.
Do paraphrase-consistency and counterfactual-separation losses each improve SingleSet’s ambiguity F1 beyond ordinary cascade-label distillation?
Removing either auxiliary loss reduces CompSplit-2 ambiguity F1 by ≥0.02 from SingleSet’s 0.86 without improving execution.
Ablate each SingleSet auxiliary loss on identical training data; bootstrap CompSplit-2 ambiguity F1 differences and compare unambiguous execution.
Ablate each SingleSet auxiliary loss using training-only labels; bootstrap CompSplit-2 F1 and execution against full model and cascade audit.
Ablations scored 0.83/0.84 F1 (execution 91%); full SingleSet disagreed with baseline on 8% of unambiguous inputs despite matching accuracy.
Defer SingleSet deployment despite 0.86 F1: it changes 8% of unambiguous baseline outputs; retain the cascade pending preservation fixes.
Add baseline-output anchoring to SingleSet and baseline fallback; tune on training folds, then retest CompSplit-2 F1 and unambiguous disagreement.
Train baseline-anchored SingleSet using training folds; apply fallback, then compare CompSplit-2 predictions against the locked cascade audit.
Anchored SingleSet v2 checkpoint includes training-fold baseline-output anchoring, frozen fallback thresholds, and CompSplit-2 prediction logs.
Audit v2’s CompSplit-2 ambiguity F1, unambiguous execution, and baseline-output disagreement against gold sets and cascade’s 0.85/91%.
On CompSplit-2, anchored SingleSet v2 scored 0.84 F1, 91% execution, and 2% baseline-output disagreement; cascade retained 0.85/91%.
Retain the cascade: SingleSet v1 changes 8% of baseline outputs; anchored v2 reduces disagreement but misses 0.85 F1.
